proofs_and_methods: Terminal debt/equity allocation is proved by cases under the stated nonrecourse, no-other-claim, no-interim-distribution, no-workout-cost baseline. Cost intervention explicitly accounts for destroyed assets rather than paying them twice.

Conditional debt concavity and equity convexity proof is valid for a finite nonnegative Q-distributed asset, with strictness when positive mass crosses face. Preserving only a P mean does not establish price preservation.

Survival recursion conditions on the remaining population; first-default masses telescope. The exponential derivation requires deterministic regular hazard, positive survival and no initial default atom. It is not asserted as a general stochastic-intensity factorization.

Recovery-at-default integration discounts recovery against first-default density and survival principal separately. The removable r+lambda singularity, zero intensity/recovery and negative-rate timing cases follow without an untaught stochastic-calculus theorem.

Market-value recovery uses its own short-step pricing relation, differentiable pre-default value and terminal condition. Its adjusted rate r+lambda(1-rho) is not substituted for a fractional-par contract.

Matrix powers assume homogeneous Markov transitions and an initially live claim. Absorbing default encodes history, and only first entry earns recovery. Common P/Q support is enforced; exhausted future survivor hazards are null.

Two-name Frechet bounds follow from four nonnegative cells. Covariance and tranche formulas preserve marginals and resources. Correlation needs nonzero marginal variances and is not claimed to determine arbitrary larger-portfolio tails.

Liquidity multiplier is a stipulated nonreplicable/frictional benchmark premise. The chapter never posits two unrestricted executable prices for identical dated claims, and one quote does not identify hazard/recovery/liquidity or a physical default law.
